You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The test case `testStripLeadingAndTrailingQuotes` verifies that the Util.stripLeadingAndTrailingQuotes method returns the input string unchanged if it does not start and end with quotes at the exact ends.

From the code snippet of Util.stripLeadingAndTrailingQuotes:
- It checks if the input string starts with a double quote (").
- If yes, it removes the first character (substring from index 1 to end).
- It then checks if the resulting string ends with a double quote.
- If yes, it removes the last character (substring from 0 to length-1).
- Returns the possibly trimmed string.

This function therefore tries to strip exactly one leading quote character at the beginning and one trailing quote character at the end, if they exist.

The issue, as described in the current bug report, is that this stripping is done blindly to all argument values, leading to unexpected removal of quotes that are not both leading and trailing. The example in the bug report:
`--balloo "this is a \"test\""` results in the value `this is a "test` (missing the trailing quote) after processing, when it should keep the trailing quote.

This matches what the method does currently:
- If the argument starts with a quote, it removes that one character.
- Then if it ends with a quote, it removes that character.
- But in the example `this is a "test"`, the string passed to the method will likely be `"this is a \"test\""` (surrounded by quotes from shell parsing).
- The method will remove the first leading quote.
- Then also remove the trailing quote - even if the quote at the end is actually escaped or part of the argument and not a simple literal trailing quote.

The test case's assert:
`assertEquals("foo \"bar\"", Util.stripLeadingAndTrailingQuotes("foo \"bar\""));`
Requests that if the input does NOT have literal leading and trailing quotes, it should not modify the string.
But the method implementation is naive and strips leading and trailing quotes without checking if they are escaped or part of the string content.

The reason for the failure is the incorrect logic implemented in stripLeadingAndTrailingQuotes that can strip quotes incorrectly.

None of the recent bug reports mention this exact issue and seem unrelated.

Diagnosis:
- Method `Util.stripLeadingAndTrailingQuotes` has a naive logic that blindly strips one leading and one trailing double quote character if present.
- This behavior causes problems when argument values contain internal unescaped quotes or only a leading or only a trailing quote, which should not be stripped.
- The failing test case confirms the method does not handle these cases properly.
- The issue is aggravated by usage in Parser.processArgs, which applies this stripping to all arguments, causing broken argument values.
- The root cause is a faulty assumption in `stripLeadingAndTrailingQuotes` that any leading and trailing quote characters should be removed blindly.
- The fix requires improving the logic to correctly identify really quoted strings or avoid stripping quotes if they are escaped or partial.

This explains the test failure and matches the bug report's description.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug arises from the method Util.stripLeadingAndTrailingQuotes, which naively strips a leading and a trailing double quote character (") if they exist in the argument string without considering if these quotes are escaped or integral parts of the string. The failing test case demonstrates that the method improperly removes quotes inside strings that are not truly quoted from start to end, causing unexpected trimming of the value. The current bug report confirms that the method leads to broken argument values when Parser.processArgs applies it to all arguments blindly. None of the recent bug reports are directly related. The root cause is the method's overly simplistic logic to remove quotes regardless of context, causing it to strip trailing quotes that should be preserved. The solution requires refining the logic in stripLeadingAndTrailingQuotes to handle only proper leading and trailing quotes and respect escaped or partial quotes.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
